items.difficulty_reason: Counted unit is Lemma 7.5.12 at source lines 1265-1276: for f:A->B, families P over A and Q over B and a fibre-wise n-connected family g:P(a)->Q(f(a)), the induced map phi on total spaces is n-connected if f is, and conversely if phi is n-connected and Q is fibre-wise merely inhabited then f itself is. The author's proof (source lines 1278-1294) is not a formal consequence of the neighbouring postcomposition criterion: it computes the n-truncated fibre of phi over (b,v) as a nested sum, uses that the inner n-truncation can be absorbed because trunc n of a type is an n-type so that the sum becomes exactly trunc n (hfib f b), and then observes that contractibility transfers both ways; the converse is where the merely-inhabited hypothesis enters, through the fact that contractibility of a truncation is a mere proposition.
